source.title: Forking: Sudden Overfitting Under Replay
source.authors: Shan-Bin Yu; Shao-Yang Guo; Hao-Ran Zhao; Dan-Ni Yu; Zi-Ming Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions double descent in passing, but studies replay-induced overfitting with n-gram memory rather than testing any of the listed double-descent versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures validation loss and train–validation gaps during replay, plus effects of corpus size, table capacity, and masking. These findings concern replay-induced forking, not the listed double-descent curves. The mention of double descent is incidental. Results from cited work and hyperparameter-selection screens are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Double descent appears only in the abstract, which lists forking as a phenomenon 'in addition to grokking and double descent'; neither original source is in the reference list. No experiment sweeps model size, epochs or sample size looking for a fall-rise-fall test-error curve. The 20-epoch no-gram run (validation minimum at epoch 7, then rising) shows only one minimum and rise, with no second descent. The corpus-size sweep reports the train–validation gap shrinking, not test error rising with more data near an interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that replay plus n-gram over-encoding causes forking, a sharp train–validation separation at epoch boundaries. They attribute it to replay sharpening seen continuations and suppressing novel ones within weakly interacting context subspaces, with rare contexts contributing most of the gap. Larger corpora and low-frequency masking mitigate it. Forking also appears in a DeepSeek-style Engram model and in replayed continued-training and RLVR-like proxies. They add a caution that components proposed by autoresearch agents can have unexpected failure modes.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates replay-driven overfitting in n-gram-memory models; it does not reproduce or adapt a double-descent method.
record.method_sensitivity: Forking varies with n-gram injection route, table capacity, corpus size, replay duration, and frequency-mask threshold. Low-frequency masking and freezing or reseeding memory also alter the measured gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Replay with over-encoding n-gram memory produces a staircase train–validation gap aligned with epoch boundaries. Larger corpora and low-frequency retrieval masking reduce the gap; larger tables increase it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under data replay, n-gram over-encoding amplifies a replay-aligned train–validation gap ('forking'), concentrated in rare contexts.

fits_no_version.finding: No-gram control overfits slowly under 20-epoch replay: validation loss is lowest at epoch 7 (3.31 nats) and higher afterwards (3.564 at epoch 20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prolonged replay on a fixed corpus eventually raises validation loss even without memory modules, with a much smaller gap.

record.problems: Most core comparisons use seed 42; the main measurement is validation loss or a train–validation gap rather than downstream test performance. The fixed single-shard training corpus and fixed validation pool limit scope. A no-gram control for the DeepSeek-style model failed to train, preventing that comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No other directly relevant reported outcomes were left out. Cited results from related work and optimizer/hyperparameter-selection screens were excluded because they do not report a direct test of the listed double-descent versions.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; table-capacity sweep (R5) reports gap only, with no interpolation threshold.
Epoch trajectories (R1–R3, R10) show monotonic gap growth or a single validation minimum, with no second descent tested.
Corpus-size sweep (R4) reports gap decreasing with data, not test error near an interpolation threshold.
No label-noise, multiple-peak or tuned-regularization tests.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to 'none' with state cannot_determine. The double-descent mention is a passing analogy in the abstract, not an engagement with the claim. 'cites_only' is retained even though the original papers are not formally cited.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep measuring test error around an interpolation threshold.
Replay-epoch validation-loss trajectories are measured, but the paper does not test the claimed fall-rise-fall double-descent shape.
Corpus size is varied, but the reported outcome is the train–validation gap, not test error near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison of double descent across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across axes.
No test of label-noise or regularization dependence, multiple descent peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No effective-parameter recounting of a double-descent curve.

rows.subject: both-table model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768; 220 rows per bigram and trigram table
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 20 replay epochs on the fixed single-shard corpus

conditions.value: fixed single-shard corpus, 337 updates per pass

rows.measure: Epoch-end online train–validation gap and fixed-validation cross-entropy
rows.value: At epoch 20, raw gap 12.674 nats and validation loss 12.779 nats; epoch-end gaps increase monotonically over 20 epochs.
rows.note: Reports replay-associated forking, not a model-size or double-descent test.

rows.subject: trigram-only model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768; 220-row trigram table
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 20 replay epochs on the fixed single-shard corpus

conditions.value: fixed single-shard corpus, 337 updates per pass

rows.measure: Epoch-end online train–validation gap and fixed-validation cross-entropy
rows.value: At epoch 20, raw gap 15.552 nats and validation loss 16.103 nats; the trigram-only net gap grows approximately linearly over passes 5–20, slope 0.664 per pass, R2 = 0.998.
rows.note: Authors caution that the finite-window fit does not establish unbounded long-run growth.

rows.subject: no-gram model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768; no n-gram tables
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 20 replay epochs on the fixed single-shard corpus

conditions.value: fixed single-shard corpus, 337 updates per pass

rows.measure: Epoch-end fixed-validation cross-entropy and online train–validation gap
rows.value: Validation loss is lowest at epoch 7 (3.31 nats) and rises afterwards; at epoch 20 validation loss is 3.564 nats and raw gap is 1.012 nats.
rows.locator: Appendix D, Figure 17 and accompanying text
rows.note: The control also overfits slowly under this replay regime.

rows.subject: trigram-only model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768; 220-row trigram table
rows.operation_detail: Varied training-corpus size over 20 sizes
rows.measure: Epoch-2 and epoch-3 end online train–validation gaps
rows.baseline: Smaller corpora; exact comparison values not stated
rows.value: Both epoch-end gaps fall by more than an order of magnitude as corpus size grows, reaching 0.13 and 0.22 nats at 20D1, respectively.
rows.note: The paper reports gap, not test error as a function of sample size.

rows.subject: bigram-only and trigram-only models
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768; table capacity varied across three decades
rows.operation_detail: Varied n-gram table row capacity
rows.value: The gap generally increases sublinearly on log–log axes as table rows increase; the bigram curve flattens toward the upper end of the measured range.
rows.note: This varies memory-table capacity, not overall network size, and measures the gap rather than test error.

rows.subject: input-, attention-value-, and attention-output-injection models
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; hidden width 768
rows.operation_detail: Compared replay-associated train–validation loss trajectories across n-gram injection routes and a no-gram model

conditions.value: input, attention value (v), attention output (y), no-gram

rows.baseline: No-gram model described as having a small gap by comparison
rows.value: All three over-encoding routes fork; attention routes (v, y) fork more strongly than input; no-gram gap stays small by comparison.
rows.note: Qualitative replay-gap comparison, not a double-descent test.

conditions.value: novel continuations after training-seen bigram contexts

rows.value: No-gram control improves to 5.6 nats; both-table model deteriorates from 7.5 to 9.0 nats.
rows.note: Authors describe this as aggregate evidence for a replay-associated novel-continuation penalty, not a claim that each context follows the same trajectory.
